title: SessionStart
description: Opens a session on a workspace. The path is checked against the allowlist before anything else happens — it is the first line of defence, not a hint.

x-required-when.because: a fork point is a message of a conversation, and only a resumed conversation has one

workspacePath.description: Absolute path of the workspace. Outside the allowlist it is refused with WORKSPACE_NOT_ALLOWED, and a root that exists but belongs to someone else answers 404, never 403.

model.description: Model to open with. Absent means the server default.

permissionMode.description: The canonical mode (plan 28, D-16): `ask` — every call that needs leave asks; `acceptEdits` — file edits are accepted, the rest asks; `readOnly` — nothing changes: the server refuses every write and every shell, whatever the engine thinks; `allowAll` — Permitir tudo, ours: the server allows every call no rule refuses, but questions and plans (ADR-022). Only the modes the engine announces in `capabilities.permissionModes` are offered. The previous protocol named them `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan` and `allowAll`, and its `bypassPermissions` is refused.

effort.description: How much effort the model puts in, for the whole session. Absent is the installation's default. Chosen before the session exists, because changing it on a live one (`applyFlagSettings`) restarts the CLI's query and drops its hooks — measured in plan 08, D-16. A level the model does not take is `INVALID_INPUT` (`session.error.effortUnsupported`). An enum read as a string, so a level added later does not break a client. Only a level the engine announces in `capabilities.effortLevels` — any other is `INVALID_INPUT`.

engine.description: The engine to open on — an `id` of `GET /engines`. Absent for the installation's default. Ignored by a resume, which opens on the engine of the conversation it continues.

resumeFrom.description: The conversation to continue instead of starting fresh. Checked by the engine's own rule before anything is spawned: an engine that is not enabled, or an id it never hands out, is `INVALID_INPUT`.

forkAt.description: Edit and resend: the `messageId` of the user prompt to rewrite. The conversation `resumeFrom` names continues from **just before** it, always in a new id — the original stays as it was (plan 08, D-19). A point the conversation does not have is `INVALID_INPUT` (`session.error.forkPointUnknown`); one the CLI refuses is `SESSION_FORK_REJECTED`.
